target: arbitrary w in W_K(A_gen), where dim_Q W_K=2 and W_K is disjoint from the generic divisor-generated degree-six line

candidate_families.reason: For the very-general target NS_Q=Q[E], the codimension-3 divisor algebra is Q[E^3], lying in the K-isotypic (3,3 exterior-count) summand, while W_K lies in the (6,0)+(0,6) K-isotypic summands. The intersection is zero.
They live on the split [-1] component and standard K-compatible transport to [-3] is blocked by discriminant invariance. Importing the known cycle by name would violate target leakage.

candidate_families.required_equality: Exceptional projection of ch_3(E) must be a nonzero class in W_K(A_gen); to solve arbitrary input, a source-generated algebraic family must span W_K or use the algebraic K-action to generate the K-line from one nonzero Weil class.
The correspondence must be defined algebraically on the target component and send an explicitly algebraic source class to the declared w (or a spanning family) in W_K.

hard_block.missing_object: one nonzero target-side algebraic codimension-3 class in W_K(A_gen), or an algebraic family/correspondence that produces one
hard_block.unblock_condition: Construct such a class with exact cohomological equality. Once one nonzero Weil class is algebraic, the algebraic K-action can be tested as a route to the full two-dimensional rational Weil space, but that implication must be proved in the returned source geometry rather than assumed.

forbidden_inference: Absolute-Hodge, Mumford-Tate, or Hodge-type status alone is not treated as algebraicity.
